text: Both surfaces work and both teams trust them -- which means this platform now needs to survive without us standing next to it. Three documents make that possible.

A plain-English dictionary entry for Package Status, a prose lineage from the scanners and GPS trackers through Kafka to both the batch and real-time paths, and an on-call runbook for the one question that matters at 3am: where do I look first.

The dictionary entry earns its keep on what it excludes -- this is not a live GPS location, not a sub-second guarantee, and not a proof-of-delivery record. That's what stops someone quietly reinterpreting the field six months from now.

The runbook is a decision tree, not a reference manual: check Kafka, then the Eventstream, then the Eventhouse -- and it explicitly rules out the batch Structured Streaming job, which has nothing to do with this path.
This platform can now be handed off. One video left: the honest ending.
